purpose: Analyzer-vs-analyzer parity on shared constructs. The two web-family ruling memos (dup-key, #813/#814) were both found by family-wide precedent probes, never by a lane or a per-language review: F5 compares one analyzer against its own oracle, site-agnostically (label+target, never the source), so a divergence BETWEEN analyzers is invisible to it by construction. Every value below was emitted live by the analyzers at the commit that introduced this file.
coverageBoundary: 13 analyzers carry a snippet for `member-read-through-receiver` (the managed-OO + receiver languages). ruby/objc/haskell/c/zig/groovy/vue/svelte are deliberately OUT of this construct's scope and are NOT declared here — the gate fails on an undeclared snippet and on a snippetless declaration, so widening coverage is a deliberate act rather than silence.

member-read-through-receiver.description: a read of an own member through the receiver (this/self/$this/s.) from inside a method
member-read-through-receiver.declaredAt: M49 W15 (#813/#814 rulings, commits 35a51bfa + this wave); kotlin's GAP re-adjudicated at M49 W20 (see its note); the `edgeTargetSpelling` axis added 2026-10-15 (task-135) after dart and php were found to be publishing this member QUALIFIED while the gate reported `observed "none"` — an edge that exists is not an absent edge

dart.note: MEASURED 2026-10-15 (task-135): dart publishes the tracked member QUALIFIED in BOTH edges it emits for this construct — `uses read -> Store.count` and `contains Store -> Store.count` (confidence 0.9). That is the spelling the fleet's own dart `contains` ruling REQUIRES (`script/m14/oracles/dart-contains.ts`: `symbol.scope ? `${symbol.scope}.${symbol.name}` : symbol.name`), because a bare member name repeated across a project is ambiguous by construction. The gate previously reported `observed "none"` for this lane because its matcher accepted only the bare spelling, so an edge that EXISTED was indistinguishable from no edge at all; fixed in verify-family-parity.ts, which now finds it under either spelling and pins the spelling here.

php.note: MEASURED 2026-10-15 (task-135): php publishes this member under TWO SPELLINGS IN THE SAME FILE — `uses read -> Store.count` (qualified, confidence 0.9) and `contains Store -> count` (bare). Both edges name the same member of the same class. This is an INTERNAL inconsistency in the php analyzer and is recorded here as a NAMED OPEN DEFECT rather than gated: this construct tracks the read-through-receiver edge, and pinning its spelling here makes a future flip visible, but the contains-vs-uses disagreement needs an owner decision on the published spelling and is NOT asserted by this check. It was previously INVISIBLE — the old matcher reported `observed "none"`, so php looked like a lane with no edge rather than one with two spellings.

kotlin.note: RE-ADJUDICATED at M49 W20 (#740 -> fixed). This was declared a GAP on purpose, with the instruction that if kotlin starts emitting the gate must fire and the gap be re-adjudicated rather than silently become a divergence. It fired, and this is that re-adjudication: kotlin now observes source=read, symbolName=count, confidence 0.6 for `this.count` inside a method — the same shape as java/scala/every other declared language, so the construct is no longer a divergence and the gap declaration is retired. The gap's own negative control still exists in verify-family-parity.ts (`rule rejects a gap that now emits`), so the rule that caught this stays able to fire.

private-member-declared-name.description: the graph name of a `#`-private member: the declared symbol spelling must be the one every reading edge targets (M49 W15 #813 ruling: the symbol keeps its declared `#` name)

java.reason: java has no `#` private-member syntax: a private member is declared `private int x` and is stored under its plain name, so there is no second spelling to reconcile.

swift.reason: swift has no `#` private-member syntax (privacy is a `private` modifier), so there is no declared-spelling/second-name split to reconcile.

kotlin.reason: kotlin has no `#` private-member syntax (privacy is a modifier); the language's member-read gap is tracked separately as #740.

scala.reason: scala has no `#` private-member syntax (privacy is a modifier); its member-read gap is tracked separately.

python.reason: python privacy is a naming convention (a leading underscore), not a distinct declared spelling.

dart.reason: dart privacy is library-scoped (`_` prefix), not a distinct declared spelling.

cpp.reason: cpp has no `#` private-member syntax; `private:` is a modifier and the name is unchanged.

csharp.reason: csharp has no `#` private-member syntax; `private` is a modifier and the name is unchanged.

php.reason: php has no `#` private-member syntax; `private` is a modifier and the name is unchanged.

go.reason: go privacy is package-scoped by capitalization, not a distinct declared spelling.

rust.reason: rust privacy is module-scoped (`pub`), not a distinct declared spelling.
